title: Chef Isaac Toups Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
description: A Cajun gumbo built on a dark milk-chocolate roux, with roasted chicken thighs and andouille simmered for three hours and served over rice.

items.note: or another smoked sausage, cut into 0.5-inch half-moons

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Season the chicken thighs with 2 teaspoons of salt and 1 teaspoon of black pepper. Place on a rimmed baking sheet, skin side up, and roast for 20 minutes, until the skin is lightly browned. Set aside and keep the rendered fat — it goes into the gumbo later.

In a heavy Dutch oven over medium heat, make a dark roux with the oil and flour, about 45 minutes. Once the roux is the color of milk chocolate, add the onion, bell pepper, and celery and stir every 5 seconds for about a minute, until the vegetables begin to soften and caramelize. The roux is rocking hot, so they cook quickly. Add the garlic and bay leaves and cook another 30 seconds, stirring frequently.

Deglaze the pot with the beer, scraping the bottom with a wooden spoon until the browned bits release, stirring constantly until it returns to a simmer. Add the stock and stir until it simmers again. Add the remaining 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon black pepper, and the cayenne. Add the reserved chicken thighs with their fat and the sausage. Bring to a bare simmer without letting it boil or the roux scorch, reduce to the lowest heat, and cover. Simmer 3 hours, stirring and scraping the bottom every 30 minutes. It should thicken but not like gravy; thin with a little water if it gets too thick.
Do not skim that fat off the top.
Serve with rice — gumbo in the bowl first, rice on top. Garnish with sliced green onions. For more heat, add another dash of Louisiana Liquid Snake.
